Since \(x\mid (7^1+12\cdot1-1)=18\), we must have \(x\le 18\).

Now check \(18\): note \(7^3\equiv 1 \pmod{18}\), so \(7^y\) cycles with period \(3\), and \(12y\pmod{18}\) also depends on \(y\pmod 3\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
y\pmod 3 & 7^y\pmod{18} & 12y\pmod{18} & 7^y+12y-1\pmod{18}\\
\hline
0 & 1 & 0 & 0\\
1 & 7 & 12 & 0\\
2 & 13 & 6 & 0
\end{array}
\]

Thus \(18\mid 7^y+12y-1\) for every natural \(y\). Therefore the largest possible \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
